name: Bhutan
summary: Bhutan's Income Tax Act 2025 took effect on 1 January 2026: progressive personal rates up to 30% above Nu 3.5M, dividends above Nu 300,000 taxed at 10%, and (per press reports of the Act) no capital gains tax on individuals' non-business assets. No wealth, inheritance or gift tax was found. Practically, Bhutan offers no residence route for a wealthy foreign family; the Gelephu Mindfulness City special region is still being set up. Research is thin (no Big-4 summary exists): low confidence.

regimes.name: Bhutan tax residence
regimes.description: Income Tax Act of Bhutan 2025: 10% on dividends above Nu 300,000; gains on personal assets reportedly untaxed.
regimes.eligibility: Tax residence under the Income Tax Act 2025 (test not verified). Foreigners rarely obtain long-term residence.

capital_gains.summary: Press reports on the Income Tax Act of Bhutan 2025 (in force 1 January 2026) state there is no capital gains tax for individuals selling personal assets outside business use. Treatment of listed shares, foreign securities and real estate was not confirmed from the Act.

capital_gains.rate_basis: Scored 0 for securities and private shares on the basis of the reported 'no CGT on personal assets'. Real estate left null: not verified (a property transfer tax existed under the old law).

dividends.summary: Dividends up to Nu 300,000 a year are exempt and dividends above are taxed at 10% (Income Tax Act 2025, as passed by the National Assembly; 10% TDS on dividends for resident and non-resident individuals per the DRC notification).

dividends.treaty_network: Very limited (treaties with India and Bangladesh reported; not verified).

routes.name: No investor residence route
